correctness.rationale: For a nonconstant binary quasinecklace the defining tie-break is automatic: each longest zero run is followed by 1, and the word ends with 1. Remove its initial 0^ℓ1; splitting the remaining suffix at ones gives exactly the (possibly empty) composition of n−ℓ−1 with parts at most ℓ+1. Adding the two constants proves the exact formula, including n=1. A nonempty suffix contributes x_{n,ℓ}=n2^(−ℓ−2) times the fair-bit probability of no ℓ+1 consecutive zeros with the final bit fixed at 1. For r=ℓ+1, two starts of 10^r within distance r are incompatible; separate starts are independent. Counting separated h-tuples gives binomial(M−r(h−1),h)2^(−h(r+1)), M=t−r−1, and Bonferroni gives exp(−x) at a fixed phase and offset. The initial boundary-run event is O(2^−r). In the lower tail disjoint blocks of 2^(r+2) bits each have probability >1/2 of an internal occurrence by the stated second-moment bound; this gives an exponentially summable tail in x. The upper tail is geometric in ℓ−floor(log₂ n). Burnside gives N₂(n)~2^n/n; the phase approximation holds over all n by compactness of the phase circle and the uniform tail estimates. The profile extends holomorphically to |Im θ|<π/(2 ln 2) by local uniform convergence, proving real analyticity. Unfolding the periodization gives the stated gamma coefficients and |c₁|≈7.13011726×10⁻⁶; hence many phase subsequences and no scalar ratio limit. Independently counted maximal circular zero-run starts over every binary word at lengths 2–11 (python -B /workspace/independent_checks.py 4). That finite check tests the counting equivalence, not the asymptotic.

evidence: In that proof, with r=C=1/2 and x_m=n2^−m, the probability of exactly k largest parts equals Σ_m exp(−x_m)(x_m/2)^k/k!+o(1) for each fixed k. After multiplication by k and summation this gives Σ_m(x_m/2)exp(−x_m/2), exactly the proposed phase function with m=ℓ+1. The Poisson approximants have uniformly bounded second moment because the second-moment series is Σ_m exp(−x_m/2)(x_m/2+x_m²/4), a bounded lattice sum.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For the real multiplicity T, bound its first and second factorial moments by summing over q=1 or 2 marked maximal zero-run starts of length ℓ. Compatible marked starts require disjoint ℓ-zero strings and precede each by 1, giving probability ≤2^(−qℓ). If ℓ≤floor(log₂ n), remove those marked positions and split the remaining fair bits (at most two intervals) into 2^(ℓ+3)-bit blocks. Each has probability >1/2 of an occurrence of 10^(ℓ+1) by the second-moment bound for this nonoverlapping-start pattern. Requiring none gives at most C exp(−c n2^−ℓ). Thus these factorial-moment contributions are bounded by C(n2^−ℓ)^q exp(−c n2^−ℓ) below the window and by (n2^−ℓ)^q above, both uniformly summable. Constants contribute O(n²2^−n). Hence E T²=O(1), also conditional on the last bit being 1, and both distributions' first moments follow by truncating k, using the earlier fixed-k formulas and removing truncation. The rotation-bias estimate then transfers the conclusion to E T and Burnside to Q₂/N₂. The Fourier formula is the direct transform of that same prior lattice profile.

evidence: The exact-content record identifies admissible rotation origins with maximal cyclic zero runs (in the primitive period for distinct rotations). Counting each origin as a labeled index, including n for each constant word, gives E T=nQ₂(n)/2^n for iid circular bits. Conditional on the last bit being 1, the zero gaps split into parts 0^(m−1)1 of a uniform composition of n, so T counts its largest parts (including n when all bits are ones).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Rotation invariance gives E[T | last bit=1]=E[(2K/n)T] where K is the Binomial(n,1/2) number of ones. Once E[T²] is bounded, the difference from E T is O(n^−1/2) by Cauchy–Schwarz. This is a multiplicity-of-the-maximum statistic, not merely the distribution of the longest run.

originality.rationale: The exact count is equivalent to earlier fixed-content enumeration summed over content. More decisively, the nonconstant unrestricted overhead law is a corollary of Bender–Canfield–Gao's published asymptotic distribution of the multiplicity of the maximum part of a uniform composition. The correspondence between quasinecklaces and maximal cyclic zero runs also appears in the earlier exact-content Resultary record. The transfer from fixed terminal bit to circular fair bits and from fixed-multiplicity probabilities to the first moment needs a tail check, supplied below. This is mathematical coverage, not a conclusion from a similarly titled result or an attempted but inaccessible source.
residual_risks: This does not assert that the algorithmic ratio was previously printed in the same form; coverage is demonstrated by reduction to an older statistic and theorem.
